title: 2D physics: Wake bodies on constraint removal

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #64890

## Additional information

This PR wakes bodies when constraints are removed, for example, a platform that moves away from a sleeping body will wake the body, rather than leave it floating. 

This draft is part of a larger effort to solve this problem across all Godot physics engines for 3.x and 4.x.

This fix is more carefully considered than the one it replaces (#121748). 

It will only wake a neighboring body if it was actually touching that body before it moved away or was freed. As far as I can think through, this is an optimal approach for what it is doing and it is hard to imagine a meaningfully faster way of doing this without having some special knowledge of the system being simulated.

Waking neighbouring bodies like this is a small cost of following two pointers to objects that are already being touched by the CPU during constraint removal or after a narrow phase collision result between the two bodies reports that they are not touching. 

However, the larger cost of waking bodies is that there are more bodies to simulate. In Godot Physics, the Islands are built based on broad phase results rather than narrow phase. When one body is woken, the whole island is woken, and Godot Physics is making those islands too large. Still the bigger problem with this is that per-frame constraint processing cannot be well threaded. The only answer I currently see to this problem is a minor refactor of Godot Physics.

Another large cost is how long bodies are woken for. There is potential for further optimization here, but it is more of a simulation math problem and user interface problem than it is book keeping.

One last performance issue that has been previously discussed is what happens when you dispose of a large amount of bodies all at once. As far as I can analyze, the cost of this waking logic should be next to zero cost in that case (compared to the other work going on...most notably removal from the BVH). The cost is that you are touching 2 bodies for every constraint removed, so I can't see any way that blows out, given that the waking operation just sets some flags. Those flags don't do meaningful work unless the bodies are subsequently simulated in the physics step...but the bodies will have left the physics space and the BVH before that happens. 

Having said all this, the control flow can be complex, with plenty of side effects worth double checking and testing.

## Testing
Tested on my own game and prototype as well as the MRP from #64890 

Additionally, edit the #64890 MRP so that the CharacterBody2D moves rather than being removed.
